keySentence: Pinocchio told lies to avoid consequences but every lie made his situation progressively worse.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Pinocchio's story follows a clear and painful pattern. He makes a small mistake and then lies to cover it up. The lie creates a new problem larger than the first. He lies again to escape that and the next problem is even bigger. By the time he reaches the shark's belly he is completely lost. None of his troubles came from real wickedness or cruelty. They all came from choosing small lies to avoid small discomforts. Pinocchio told lies to avoid consequences but every lie made his situation progressively worse.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: Pinocchio's story follows a very clear and very painful pattern from beginning to end. He makes a small mistake and then tells a lie to cover it and avoid being found out. The lie creates a new problem that is larger and more serious than the original mistake. He tells another lie to escape the new problem and creates an even larger problem still. By the time he reaches the belly of the shark he is far from home and completely lost. None of his troubles came from a single act of genuine wickedness or cruelty toward others. They all came from the small and repeated choice to avoid discomfort with a convenient untruth. Pinocchio told lies to avoid consequences but every lie made his situation progressively worse.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: Pinocchio's entire story follows a very clear and very painful pattern, and the pattern repeats itself with almost mathematical regularity from beginning to end. He makes a small and entirely ordinary mistake — skipping school, losing some books, believing something he should not have believed. Then he tells a lie to cover up the mistake and to avoid being found out by Geppetto or by the fairy who watches over him. The lie itself creates a new problem that is larger and far more serious than the original small mistake had ever been. He then tells another lie in order to escape from the new problem, and the second lie creates an even larger and more dangerous problem still. By the time he eventually reaches the cold and terrifying belly of the great shark, he is far from home and completely lost in every possible sense. None of his troubles, if you trace them back carefully, came from a single act of real wickedness or genuine cruelty toward any other person. They all came instead from the small, repeated, almost invisible choice to avoid a moment of discomfort by telling one more convenient untruth. Pinocchio told lies to avoid consequences but every lie made his situation progressively worse.
facts.Word cards: progressively = 점점 더 / situation = 상황 / avoid = 피하다 / honesty = 정직함
